verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev has dedicated first-party self-hosting docs: running the platform on your own infrastructure with full control, plus a Docker guide with a simplified `docker compose up` setup. llms.txt describes it as an open-source platform. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment, and evidence on production-grade options (e.g., Kubernetes or scaling guidance) beyond Docker.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Self-hosting Trigger.dev means you run and manage the platform on your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your environment, deployment process, and the URLs you expose the service on.
You can self-host Trigger.dev on your own infrastructure using Docker.
No more startup scripts, just `docker compose up`.
Open source platform for durable, long-running tasks.
